Hold and **fix first** on **PR 1763 + 1755 (interiors and wounds)**, **PR 1782 (rocks)**, **PR 1776 (planets)**, **PR 1730 (acid cook-off)**, and **PR 1772 (stations and hulks)** before Ryan's look picks. ## 3. Row-by-Row Visual Review

### Row 1: `1763_1755_interiors` (PR 1763 / #1743 and PR 1755 / #1741)
- **Pick: Fix first.**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - In `joint_I15_11.png` and `closeups_I15_B21.png` (left), the two Glasswright breach wounds (`j_wound_I15_11__c26.png`) look like **flat, round, blurry dark-charcoal smudges with wavy grey horizontal noise stripes**. There are no crisp crystal facets, no popped mosaic panes, and no white-gold internal light cores. On `Broken (6 s after death)`, the torn hull mouth shows dull grey rocky slabs with no warm core light. At `c170` and `c26` breached top view, the wounds barely read at all.
  - In `joint_B21_11.png` and `closeups_I15_B21.png` (right), **`Broken (6 s after death), camera 26` is empty space**: both Chorus halves drifted off the top and bottom of the frame (only tiny spine tips peek at the top edge), so the Chorus broken interior is completely unproven at `c26`. In the closeup wound (`j_wound_B21_11__c26.png`), the hole sits on a dark brown cracked dome with bright **orange/amber rim outlines** along adjacent shell edges (reading like hot metal edges on a flesh hull) and a tiny green gas puff; ivory bone ribs, wet tendon strands, and pulsing bile sacs do not read. Breached (`50%`) top views look nearly identical to Intact.
  - In `interior_lineup_r420.jpg` (which still carries a stale cloud stamp `20a1b6a76128 | cloud direction check`, not `e1153b84`), `S10` (Sunward), `H10` (Directorate), `A16` (Hullbreakers), and `C11` (Chorus) cutaways read clearly and cohesively. However, `GP1` (Glasswrights) is an **overexposed tie-dye neon confetti blur** because thick unlined outer mosaic panes bleed onto the inner face, and `E12` (Eclipse) has a **bright neon-green center sphere**.
- **Claims and playbook clashes:**
  - PR 1755 claims `"no soot or black on glass"` and `docs/playbooks/deaths_and_hits.md:290-291` requires `"straight-edged crystalline fracture facets and popped mosaic panes over braided light cores glowing white-gold (zero soot, zero black holes, zero radial sine webs)"`. The dark blurry smudges on `I15_11` violate both directly.
  - `docs/playbooks/deaths_and_hits.md:275,288-289` calls for `"snapped bone ribs and wet tendon strands"` over `"muddy olive-umber hide, ivory bone hoops and pulsing yellow-green bile sacs"`. Neither reads in `closeups_I15_B21.png`.
  - `docs/playbooks/ships.md:85,103,448` requires `"all violet, no green on the hull"` and `"zero green inside"`. PR 1763 notes honestly that `E12`'s green sphere is exterior `ecore` (`CORE_RGB`) waiting on `#1422` and that `GP1`'s mosaic bleed is `ithar/hull.py` lacking an inner liner. Both still clash visually with the approved look (and `E12`'s green core appears again in Row 6 `eclipse_c26.png`).
- **Why fix first:** Metal and Chorus cutaways in PR 1763 are strong, but Wounds V2 (PR 1755) is visibly broken on Glasswrights and unreadable/unframed on Chorus, and Glasswright cutaways (`GP1`) need an inner liner (or dark inner face) before Ryan signs off. Re-capture `joint_B21_11` on top of PR 1737 so the broken halves stay inside `c26`.

### Row 2: `1782_rocks` (PR 1782 / #1361)
- **Pick: Fix first.**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - `RK1361_stone.jpg`, `RK1361_iron.jpg`, and `RK1361_carbon.jpg` are **night-and-day upgrades**. Before, all three looked like the exact same puffy tan clay potato. After, `stone` has sharp layered craggy cliffs, `iron` reads as dark pitted gunmetal with crisp metallic glints, and `carbon` reads as deep matte charcoal basalt.
  - `RK1361_crystal.jpg` removes the cartoonish glowing cyan crystal spikes, which is a big taste win.
  - **The problem:** compare `RK1361_crystal.jpg` (AFTER, "comet") directly beside `RK1361_ice.jpg` (AFTER, "ice"). Both are elongated dark charcoal ovals covered in **blurry mottled white patches that look like white paint splatter or stucco on dark grey slate**. They look almost identical to each other at both `c170` and `c26`. No translucent ice sheen, no subtle cold vent glow, and no far-edge comet gas tails appear anywhere in the five sheets.
  - Minor proof hygiene note: every BEFORE and AFTER panel stamps the exact same commit `745cf54a080f | installed in game` (only the clock changes from `10:57` to `11:05`), likely from toggling `VS_1361_OLD=1` on one install rather than capturing `main e4b7d034` as stated in `README.md`.
- **Claims and playbook clashes:**
  - PR 1782 claims `"ice frost only on the fresh shelves"`, `"comet nuclei (dark crust, sheets of white ice, a dim cold glow only in a few deep vents)"`, and `"two or three big nuclei beyond the far edge with soft anti-sun gas tails"`. None of those distinguish `crystal` from `ice` in the `ROCKS_I` captures, and the gas tails are absent.
- **Why fix first:** Stone, iron, and carbon are ready to ship today. Separate `ice` (brighter pale glacial blue-white body with sharp ice facets) from `comet` (darker carbon nucleus with crisp frost seams, dim cold vent glints, and a wide capture proving the anti-sun tails) so the two kinds do not read as twins.

### Row 3: `1776_planets` (PR 1776 / #1765)
- **Pick: Fix first.**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - `PV2-B0 rocky after`, `PV2-B1 terran after`, `PV2-B5 barren after`, `PV2-P2 after`, `PV2-P3 after`, and `PV2-M1 after` are **massive upgrades**. Rocky, terran, and barren look crisp, photorealistic, and grounded in the real battle shots (`PV2_battle.jpg` `s5`, `s6`, `s9`), and replacing neon-purple gas giant `P2` with banded slate/bronze/cream fits the game's tone completely.
  - **Blocker 1 (Ice):** `PV2-B3 ice after` (`PV2_board_c170.jpg`, `PV2_board_close.jpg`), `PV2-P6 after` (`PV2_backdrop_2.jpg`), `PV2-M3 after` (`PV2_moons.jpg`), and `PV2-s7 ice, cold` (`PV2_battle.jpg`) look **fake and distracting**. The lines meant to be Europa's tectonic lineae loop back on themselves like **brown cursive crayon scribbles ("W" and "o" loops, tangled spaghetti)** drawn on a smooth glossy plastic sphere. In `PV2_moons.jpg`, `PV2-M3 after` is also visibly **stretched vertically into an egg** (pre-existing on `M3 before`, still unfixed). In `PV2_standin.jpg`, `PV2-B3 ice stand-in` looks like half rusty desert mud and half blue cloud instead of ice.
  - **Blocker 2 (Volcanic):** `PV2-B4 volcanic after`, `PV2-P4 after`, and `PV2-s8 volcanic, cold` **no longer read as volcanic at all**. While the old lava web was too loud, the new version went all the way to a **blurry, smooth, dusty orange-brown haze ball** (softer than rocky `B0`!) with almost zero visible lava fissures, flows, or calderas even up close in `PV2_board_close.jpg`.
  - Minor note: `PV2-M0 after` (grey) and `PV2-M2 after` (basalt) look almost identical in `PV2_moons.jpg`.
- **Claims and playbook clashes:**
  - PR 1776 claims `"ice: Europa-style lineae, chaos terrain and a gloss sheen"` and `"volcanic: flows, canyon grit and fissure glow"`. Real Europa lineae are straight or gently arcing intersecting tectonic bands, never tangled loops; and volcanic shows neither readable canyon grit nor fissure glow at battle distance.
- **Why fix first:** Keep rocky, terran, barren, `P2`, and `M1` untouched, fix the ice lineae generator into crisp straight/gently-arcing cracks (plus fix `M3`'s egg stretch and `B3`'s muddy stand-in), and give volcanic dark crisp basalt ridges with restrained glowing caldera/fissure veins so players recognize it immediately.

### Row 4: `1737_wrecks` (PR 1737 / #1236)
- **Pick: Ship it.**
- **What the pictures and video show:**
  - In `WRK4-1236_dreadnought_before_after.jpg` and across all six ship classes in `WRK4-1236_before_after.mp4` (Directorate dreadnought, Sunward, Hullbreakers, Glasswrights, Chorus), BEFORE visibly shrinks broken capitals down to comical 25% scale toy boats. AFTER holds every wreck at full 1:1 scale right where it broke, with both halves drifting slightly apart and braking to a calm stop.
  - Provenance clarification: `README.md` implies `99e36a46` (Artoo's stop-turning fix) was added after capture `6ce553cb`, but PR 1737's body confirms `"After pin: 6ce553cb (99e36a46 plus the same bench files)"`, and every half stops spinning cleanly in the video.
  - Unrelated bugs visible in the clip (different PRs, not blockers here): on the Glasswright catamaran (`01:29` to `01:38`), glowing purple-white engine plumes stay firing on the dead stern half after death, and its hull snaps from rainbow mosaic to dark metal-brown slats; the Directorate dreadnought cavity is jet black because this clip predates PR 1763/1755 interiors.
- **Claims and playbook clashes:** Matches PR 1737 and `docs/playbooks/deaths_and_hits.md` ("A wreck that blocks its hex") completely.
- **Why ship it:** Cleanest, biggest visual improvement in the pack. Merging it first also fixes the drifting-out-of-frame Chorus halves seen in Row 1 (`joint_B21_11.png`).

### Row 5: `1730_acid` (PR 1730 / #1394)
- **Pick: Fix first.**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - PR 1730's two targeted fixes clearly worked: on `AD1394I_c_raider_c6.jpg`, the dark soot cloud above the Hullbreaker Raider in `before split` / `before core` is completely gone in `now split` / `now core`; on `AD1394I_h_dominion_c21.jpg`, the Directorate Dominion's signature white-blue electrical arcs fire cleanly in `now core`; and across all five ships (`warden`, `raider`, `penitent`, `harvester`, `dominion`), torn wreck faces (`now wreck`, `now settled`) now show crisp yellow-green etched acid corrosion instead of orange fire, while removing the glowing green center orb from `before tell` on Eclipse `d_harvester`.
  - **The problem (`now tell`):** On ALL FIVE sheets (`AD1394I_warden_c6.jpg`, `c_raider`, `penitent`, `d_harvester`, `h_dominion`), `now tell` shows **two soft, blurry, glowing chartreuse-green cloud puffs** sitting loosely above the armor (especially obvious on the giant Dominion hull in `AD1394I_h_dominion_c21.jpg`, where they look like two small floating green cotton puffs, alongside a brown stain patch that vanishes in `now split`).
  - Sheet layout hygiene: every sheet orders its columns `tell -> split -> wreck -> core -> settled`, so `core` shows the broken halves closer together again after `wreck` already blew them apart; none of the five sheets carry a commit stamp.
- **Claims and playbook clashes:**
  - `docs/playbooks/deaths_and_hits.md:152` states: `"the plating glows a sick yellow-green only where the acid hit (each hit a ragged patch that spreads until the hull parts)... never the soft green bloom (it read as a cloud)... no fire, no smoke, no vapour (R398)"`. The soft chartreuse puffs in `now tell` read as green clouds/vapour, directly tripping R398.
- **Why fix first:** `split`, `core`, `wreck`, and `settled` are already strong and solve 1394G's soot and big-hull arc problems cleanly. Tighten the `now tell` green puffs into crisp hull-hugging ragged corrosion patches (zero floating cloud look) before Ryan accepts.

### Row 6: `1786_ship_exteriors` (PR 1786 / #1777)
- **Pick: Ship it.** (Keep behind `VS_SHIP_LOOK_V2=0` until the solo RTX 5080 frame-time gate clears and head `700bbdc9` / `996bc09d` matches `b0768e6b`.)
- **What the pictures show:**
  - Across `sunward_c26.png`, `directorate_c26.png`, `hullbreakers_c26.png`, `chorus_c26.png`, `eclipse_c26.png`, `board_view_a_c170.png`, and `board_view_b_c170.png`, turning V2 on gives a **clean, grounded contrast and crevice-depth upgrade** with zero new artifacts. Sunward loses its chalky grey wash, Directorate panels sharpen, Hullbreakers gain richer oxblood-red depth (darker red, not muddy), Chorus chitin gets a subtle wet clearcoat lift, and **Eclipse stays crisp obsidian-violet** (the PR's feared brown-shift did not happen).
  - On `glasswrights_c26.png`, `I8_37` (champagne pearl ribbons + recessed stained glass, matching `ships.md:75-81`) gains slight depth, while `I15_11` (head-to-toe rainbow confetti) barely changes at all.
- **Cross-row clashes noticed (pre-existing on `V2 off`, NOT introduced by PR 1786):**
  - `eclipse_c26.png` and `board_view_b_c170.png` show `D21_23` (E12)'s **green central core** in both `V2 off` and `V2 on` (same `#1422` clash seen in Row 1 `interior_lineup_r420.jpg`).
  - `I15_11` clashes sharply with `I8_37` inside the same faction sheet (`glasswrights_c26.png`): `I8_37` obeys `ships.md:76-81`, whereas `I15_11` has almost no pearl ribbons and reads as loud rainbow confetti (the same noisy hull that hides wounds in Row 1).
  - Pre-1755 damage artifacts are visible on the `damaged` rows in both `V2 off` and `V2 on`: bubblegum-pink smears on Chorus `B21_11 damaged` (`chorus_c26.png`, violating `deaths_and_hits.md:289` "zero magenta"), white cobweb net on Glasswright `I15_11 damaged` (`glasswrights_c26.png`, violating `deaths_and_hits.md:291` "zero radial sine webs"), and orange inner bay on Directorate `H10_23 damaged` (`directorate_c26.png`, violating `deaths_and_hits.md:287-288` "zero orange"). These belong to Wounds V2 (PR 1755), not PR 1786.
- **Why ship it:** V2 delivers an honest visual lift across five of six factions with zero V2 regressions and stays safely switch-gated until frame-time proof lands.

### Row 7: `1772_stations` (PR 1772 / #1767)
- **Pick: Fix first.**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - **Missing station coverage:** Despite the folder name `1772_stations`, there are **zero pictures of `station_T2`** (no small 3-hex cluster, no teaching station, no lone hole, no 19-hex cluster, no biome kind-lamp light spill check). PR 1772 itself flags station size, fallback dock drums, and lamp spill as its top risks for Ryan to inspect.
  - In `10_HK_chorus_c26.png` and `12_HK0_graveyard_c170.png`, **Before (H, `494595a4`, 0.04 floor) and After (K, `e31cd839`, 0.025) look virtually identical to the naked eye**. The Chorus hulk still reads as pale khaki/tan at roughly live Chorus brightness (compare Row 6 `board_view_a_c170.png` `B21_11`), and up close at `c26` its twin round recessed brown nozzles on the pale beige rear hull read like cartoon owl eyes next to an old pre-1782 clay rock.
  - In `12_HK0_graveyard_c170.png`, two pale silver/white wrecks (lower-left center and far right) still pop brighter than everything else on the board like live ships, and `README.md` notes Sheet K is already superseded by PR head `7c7ae555` (`a86497ad` on GitHub) awaiting Sheet M for R425 (wrecks never lighter than 60% of live paint).
- **Claims and playbook clashes:** PR 1772 cannot be approved from stale Sheet K when the station half of the PR has zero pictures and the wreck-darkening change is invisible in Sheet K.
- **Why fix first:** Wait for Sheet M on the live PR head AND include the missing `station_T2` cluster, hole, and kind-lamp captures before sending to Ryan.

### Row 8: `1809_1811_ui` (PRs 1809, 1810, 1811 / #1801 to #1803)
- **Pick: Fix first (context only, not acceptance-ready).**
- **What the pictures show:**
  - First, `README.md:15` misdescribes these six JPGs as `"UI audit shots before the fixes"`. Every image header explicitly shows side-by-side **cloud lavapipe** captures comparing `BEFORE: main cbb6165a` against `AFTER: PR 1810 @ c920f7f3` and `AFTER: PR 1811 @ a86fb8a0` (`ship models are cloud placeholders`). PR 1809 (Battle HUD `#1803`) has zero screenshots here.
  - **Real improvements in AFTER:** `M2_map_stop_hover.jpg` shows clear step-by-step polish (no hover -> PR 1810 orange focus box -> PR 1811 structured stop hover card). `M1_map_route_rows.jpg` and `F1_fleet_manifest.jpg` add clean row hover shading in PR 1811. `E1_event_choices.jpg` reads cleanly.
  - **Visible UI bugs still live in AFTER (`PR 1811 @ a86fb8a0`):**
    1. `B1_boon_offer.jpg`: boxed `[4]` and `[5]` shortcut badges sit directly on top of the button labels, clipping `"Reroll the offer (25 credits, onc[4]"` and `"Decline: take 40 credits[5]"`.
    2. `Y1_shipyard.jpg`: the `"REPAIR AND REFIT"` onboarding tip card sits directly over the 4th ship column (`Iron Dusk`), hiding its stats and weapons.
    3. `M1_map_route_rows.jpg` and `F1_fleet_manifest.jpg`: hover tooltips overlap the Nemesis banner (`LENS-KEEPER DREAE`) and clip adjacent ship names (`BRIGHT CENSUR`), and `M1`'s tooltip exposes raw internal scaling math (`"their strength is about 23% of your fleet's (includes Standard AI -5%)"`).
- **Claims and playbook clashes:** `docs/playbooks/screens.md:29,36,40` forbids keycap boxes (`"No pills, key badges, glows or shadows"`, `"No key caps"`) and requires `"no overlaps at any fleet size or name length"`. `B1` violates both; `Y1` violates no overlaps. Both PR 1810 and PR 1811 also still show `FAIL: standing checks` in their runner blocks.
- **Why fix first:** Keep as context only; fix `B1`'s `[4]`/`[5]` overlap and `Y1`'s tip overlap, get standing checks green, and run real PC captures (including PR 1809 Battle HUD) before acceptance.

### Wave 1: Core Tactical Fun: Kill Rubber-Banding, Fix Pacing, Restore Agency & Readability (Highest Fun ROI)
**Goal:** Make every single battle feel crisp, fair, legible, and rewarding before adding or reshaping higher-level content.

#### 1A. Remove Dynamic Rubber-Banding & Move to Honest Fixed Encounter Curves (Fixes G1)
- **Sources:** `fleetPower()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1372-1383`), `genEnemyFleet()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1631-1644`), `startBattle()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1459-1473`), `map_intel.gd` (`godot/ui/campaign/map_intel.gd:21-58`), `tables.json` (`godot/rules/data/tables.json`) (`RAMP`, `BOSS_SCALE`).
- **Recommended Approach (Pick A):**
  - Remove `fleetPower()` budget scaling (`0.75x-1.30x`) from `genEnemyFleet()` and remove `bossFit` (`0.55x-1.0x`) from `startBattle()`.
  - Replace hidden `RAMP.thin` (`0.73/0.67/0.62`) + rubber-band math with an **explicit, fixed sector/column/tier enemy budget table** (calibrated cleanly per Sector 1, 2, 3 and Easy / Standard / Elite / Boss nodes) so repairing ships, buying Mk upgrades, and drafting strong combos strictly make you stronger against the curve.
  - Update `map_intel.gd` tooltips to show **readable encounter strength tier + enemy ship count/archetype** (never `"23% of your fleet's (includes Standard AI -5%)"`).
- **Alternative (Option B):** Keep a tiny one-way floor (`min 0.85x` protection only in Sector 1 Column 1-2 if a player lost half their fleet early), with **strictly 0% upward penalty** (`cap = 1.0`) for upgrades, repairs, boons, relics, or meta unlocks.
- **Fable Sign-Off:** Pick A (pure fixed curve like FTL/Slay the Spire) vs Option B (fixed upward, gentle Sector 1 pity floor)? Target win-rate band on Threat 0 across `playtest-and-balance` sims (e.g., 45-60% for competent play)?
- **Astra Sign-Off:** Rules determinism & saved-results impact: this intentionally changes battle enemy generation and HP baselines, requiring a coordinated re-baseline of `godot/rules/test/` saved results + 30-seed campaign balance sim verification (`playtest-and-balance` skill). Confirm zero save-file breakage for in-progress runs (store fixed encounter budget on node generation).
- **Opus Scope:** 1 Opus run + 1 balance-sim tuning pass (1-2 review rounds).

#### 1B. Battle Pacing, Camera Hygiene & Enemy Tactical Intent (Fixes G3 + G4)
- **Sources:** `battle.gd:64-67,165` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:64-166`), `_play_batch()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:1280-1378`), `_cine_wants()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:2187-2210`), `_overlay()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:3327-3452`), `aiPickActivation()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:7266`), `aiUnit()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:7499`).
- **Recommended Approach (Pick A):**
  1. **Camera stability:** Change default `cine = "key"` so `_cine_wants()` triggers ONLY on **capital/flagship kills, boss Commands, and player-flagged dramatic finishers**, NEVER on routine lances, torpedoes, or novas. Keep `"full"` as an explicit opt-in in Settings for cinematic fans.
  2. **Snappy turn tempo:** Include enemy move time inside the round speedup budget (`battle.gd:1329`), trim default `MOVE_HEX` lead-in/per-hex travel by ~25-30% at 1x speed, and add a **sticky Fast/Skip toggle** (or hold-to-fast-forward that persists across the whole enemy turn instead of resetting at `battle.gd:1370`).
  3. **Enemy Intent Telegraphing:** Pre-select the next activating enemy ship (using a pure deterministic preview call to `aiPickActivation()` + intended primary target/move goal) and render:
     - A crisp **"NEXT" badge/pip** on the next enemy ship to activate.
     - A subtle **hoverable target-intent tether** (or icon: Attack / Ram / Board / Ability) showing who that next enemy wants to hit, plus an optional toggle for all unacted enemies' primary threat.
  4. **Readable Combat Odds & Softer Section Breaks:**
     - Trim hit/crit variance extremes (e.g., damage variance `0.90-1.10` instead of `0.85-1.15`; raise base torpedo accuracy against cruisers/capitals or give torpedoes a clear armor/evasion split so big cooldown shots aren't 24% coin flips).
     - Change broken sections (`damageSection()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3396-3423`)) from permanent `off = 999` bricking into **2-turn crippled / degraded output** (e.g., `-50%` arc dmg or `off = 2`, engines `-1` speed instead of speed `1` / ev `0`) so wounded ships stay tactically playable rather than dead weight.
- **Alternative (Option B):** Keep current section-cripple permanence (`off = 999`) for high-lethality simulation flavor, and ship only Camera + Pacing + Next-Enemy Intent first.
- **Fable Sign-Off:** Confirm `cine = "key"` trigger list (kills + boss Commands only?), confirm whether section breaks should degrade (`-50%` / temporary jam) vs permanently brick (`off = 999`), and approve visual style of Enemy Intent markers under `screens.md:20-23,47-48` (`docs/playbooks/screens.md:20-48`) (strictly orders-sheet colors, no neon clutter).
- **Astra Sign-Off:** Verify deterministic read-only intent preview NEVER mutates `B` or consumes `rnd()` state (`aiPickActivation` preview must run on read-only state or copy without touching RNG stream). Verify `battle.gd` camera tests, `plan_commit_check`, and `ledger_readability_test` remain green.

    2. **Low-value micro-triggers (~25-30 minor passives that would interrupt battle flow if prompted):** rewrite their rules text and effect cleanly so they are **honest deterministic triggers** (e.g., *"Your flagship..."*, *"The nearest enemy..."*, *"Your first ship to fire..."*) instead of promising *"choose any ship"* and lying.

# Embers of the Hollow Sun: Fresh Holistic Game Audit

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This audit evaluates the live Godot 4 game in `godot/` completely fresh, ignoring past design history. Every critique is tested against one standard: **what makes a tactics roguelike genuinely fun, memorable, and impossible to put down?**

---

## 1. What Makes Tactics / Strategy Roguelikes Beloved

The games players sink hundreds of hours into (FTL, Into the Breach, Slay the Spire, XCOM 2, Hades, Battle Brothers, Cobalt Core) share six non-negotiable pillars:

1. **Readable puzzles with real agency:** You can hold the core rules in your head, read enemy threats before they hit, spot a clever line of play, and watch it work because of *your* decision, not a mystery spreadsheet or coin flip.
2. **Power fantasy and build pivots:** Run upgrades change *how* you play, not just `+8%` math. When you assemble a smart combo, the game lets you **feel** strong and stomp fights you earned.
3. **Snappy cadence and high decision-to-chore ratio:** Fast animations, stable camera framing, minimal post-fight paperwork. Almost every click is an interesting tactical or strategic decision.
4. **Honest risk, reward, and climactic bosses:** Hard nodes pay off clearly, failures feel earned (never hidden-rule traps), and sector bosses are unforgettable mechanical exams with signature patterns.
5. **Distinct identity out of the box:** Picking a new faction or commander immediately changes your turn-to-turn verbs on Battle 1, not after 15 hours of grinding.
6. **Earned "one more run" pull:** Losses feel exciting because they unlock new toys, reveal new strategies, or advance a rivalry that actually escalates.

### What Is Already Working Well (Keep This)

Before diagnosing what breaks, the game has genuinely strong bones:
- **Tactical naval DNA:** Directional firing arcs, turn-radius inertia, shared shield pool with quadrant coverage, six faction movement rules (`MOVE_RULES`), alternating activations, plan-on-ghost commit flow, and automatic enemy rout at `<= 35%` CP so fights skip tedious mop-up.
- **Audio/visual craft:** 45 bespoke hull meshes, layered SFX mix with capital-death ducking (`sfx.gd` (`godot/audio/sfx.gd:112-199`)), adaptive battle music (`music_player.gd` (`godot/music/music_player.gd:1-50`)), and a 3D sector chart.

**The core diagnosis:** The game does not lack features, content, or visual craft. Its problem is the opposite: **its own systems actively fight against player agency, power fantasy, clarity, and tempo.**

---

## 2. Where the Game Falls Apart (With Exact Source & Logic)

### 1. Dynamic rubber-banding steals your power fantasy and punishes playing well
**Why it hurts:** The core joy of a roguelike is out-building the curve. Here, playing smart, upgrading ships, collecting boons/relics, and even **repairing your hull before a fight** secretly makes the next enemy fleet bigger, while stumbling shrinks enemy fleets and bosses.

- **Source:** `fleetPower()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1372-1383`), `genEnemyFleet()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1631-1644`), `startBattle()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1459-1473`), mirrored in `map_intel.gd` (`godot/ui/campaign/map_intel.gd:21-58`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - `fleetPower()` scores your fleet from every ship's CP, **current HP fraction** (`0.4 + 0.6 * hp`), Mk level (`+12%` each), fitted refits (`+3%` each), captain rank (`+4%` each), hangars, rarity-weighted boons (`+3.5%` each), and relics (`+2.5%` each).
  - `genEnemyFleet()` scales every enemy budget by `clamp((fleetPower() / RAMP.refP[s])^0.6, 0.75, 1.30)` (`RAMP.refP = [0, 7, 12, 20]`).
  - `startBattle()` scales Sector Boss HP by `bossFit = clamp(playerStrength() / [0, 6, 9, 12][s], 0.55, 1.0)` on top of `BOSS_SCALE = [0, 0.5, 0.55, 0.7]`. A weak Sector 1 fleet can fight a boss at **27.5% base HP**, while a strong fleet is taxed with **+30% larger enemy fleets** everywhere.
  - Even permanent meta upgrades (`War chest I-III`, `Command authority I-II`, `Veteran officers`, `Founders' cache`, Mastery IV Mk II flagship in `newRun()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1394-1437`)) inflate `fleetPower()` on Turn 1 and trigger enemy scaling against you.
  - Meanwhile, non-boss enemies are secretly thinned to `62%-73%` HP and damage (`RAMP.thin = [0, 0.73, 0.67, 0.62]` at `rules.gd:1469-1473` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1469-1473`)). Instead of readable, fixed enemy threats that reward mastery, the math runs an invisible treadmill.

---

### 2. Fake player agency: dozens of Admiral Lineage skills lie to the player and play themselves
**Why it hurts:** The 24 Admiral Lineage Trees (`288` nodes, `214` unique `TREE_FX` effects) contain the game's most exciting, bespoke tactical promises ("name one enemy", "place one of your ships anywhere in your deployment zone", "swap any two ships", "hold one ship in reserve"). In real gameplay, **the player never gets to make those choices**, and several skills are hollow auto-shuffles.

- **Source:** `treeChoice()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4800-4850`), `treeDeployMove()` & `treeBattleStart()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5476-5528`), `runCommand()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5778-6008`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - `treeChoice(kind)` checks `B.get("treeChoices")`, which **no UI in the entire game ever sets** (it is only supplied by headless test fixtures in `godot/rules/test/scenarios.json`).
  - All **41 calls to `treeChoice(...)`** in `rules.gd` silently fall back to hardcoded heuristics (`enemy` = highest `maxHp`, `ship`/`reserve` = lowest HP%, `carrier` = largest hangar).
  - `swornDeploy` / `deployRead` (*"after seeing the enemy deployment, place one of your ships anywhere in your deployment zone"*) silently moves your lowest-HP ship **1 hex to the nearest open hex** (`rules.gd:5476-5489` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5476-5489`)).
  - `castCorrected` / `iterationSwap` (*"after deployment, swap the positions of any two of your ships"*) blindly swaps your first two ships `l[0]` and `l[1]` before you even see the board (`rules.gd:5494-5507` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5494-5507`)).
  - `debtsReserve` / `broodReserve` silently yank a ship off the board for Round 1 without asking which ship or which entry edge (`rules.gd:5508-5519` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5508-5519`)).
  - Only the 10 binary yes/no prompts in `TREE_MAY` and the Chorus `roles` picker ever open the HUD prompt (`rules.gd:4856-4896` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4856-4896`)).

---

### 3. Invisible modifier soup, stacked RNG, and no enemy intent telegraphing
**Why it hurts:** Tactical games feel brilliant when outcomes are legible and earned. Here, combat math buries the player under dozens of microscopic conditional modifiers, stacks four layers of randomness on top of big cooldowns, and hides what enemies are about to do next.

- **Source:** `_hitChance_raw()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:2858-2936`), `applyHit()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3258-3376`), `damageSection()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3396-3423`), `_landVolley_raw()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3724-3875`), `_overlay()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:3319-3452`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - **25+ stacked hit modifiers:** A single shot adds base acc, unit aim, range falloff, capped evasion times `evMult`, squadron penalty (`-15`), nebula (`-15`), debris (`-10`), storm (`-10`), two crew-loss penalties (`-10` under 50% crew, `-20` under 25%), stationary/motion modifiers, sync aim, Nemesis weakness, wing stance, adjacent evasion, marks, surge (`-20`), plus **19 conditional admiral-lineage branches**.
  - **Layered RNG misery:** Every shot rolls hit (`5%-95%`, `rules.gd:3621` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3621`)), damage variance (`0.85 + rnd() * 0.3`, `rules.gd:3823` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3823`)), crit (`1.5x+`, `rules.gd:3316` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3316`)), and point-defense/wing intercepts (`rules.gd:2736` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:2736`)). A flagship torpedo (`shots: 1, dmg: 42, acc: 64, evMult: 2, cd: 2`) has just **24% base hit** against a standard frigate before flak even rolls: pure feast-or-famine coin-flipping.
  - **Mid-battle death spirals from section breaks:** Each ship's prow (`30%` maxHp), mid (`45%`), and engine (`25%`) track separate HP (`rules.gd:1367` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:1367`)). Breaking a section permanently disables all forward weapons (`off = 999`), all flank weapons + shields, or drops speed to 1 and evasion to 0 (`rules.gd:3409-3420` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:3409-3420`)), turning damaged ships into helpless bricks before they die.
  - **Zero tactical enemy intent:** Aside from the 1-round boss Command warning (`rules.gd:5752` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5752`)), enemies choose which ship activates and what it does on the fly (`aiPickActivation()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:7266`), `aiUnit()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:7499`)). The board only shows generic reachable danger hatching (`danger_on` / `R` threat map), never which enemy activates next or which target it intends to focus, ram, or board.

---

### 4. Camera hijacking and sluggish cadence break flow during battle
**Why it hurts:** Great tactics games keep your eyes anchored on the board and let turns snap along at your brain's speed. Here, the camera repeatedly rips away from your view mid-fight and enemy turns drag out into passive watching.

- **Source:** `_cine_wants()` & `_play_fire()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:2179-2240`), `MOVE_HEX` / `MOVE_CAP` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:64-67`), `_play_batch()` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:1239-1378`), `swarmPhase()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:6764-6772`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - Under the default `cine = "key"` setting (`battle.gd:165` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:165`)), `_cine_wants` returns `true` for **every single lance, torpedo, and nova attack in the battle** (`"lance", "torp", "nova": return true`), plus capital volleys on flagships or low-HP targets and almost all ship kills (`size >= 0.6`). Each cut-in swings the camera side-on, adds letterbox bars, pauses `320ms` before firing, and snaps back. A single fight involving Glasswrights, Eclipse, or Crusade cruisers/destroyers hijacks the player's camera **10 to 20 times**.
  - Ships move one at a time at `560-860ms` per hex plus `250-450ms` lead-in (up to `7.0s` per move), and enemy move time is explicitly excluded from the round speedup budget (`battle.gd:1329` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:1329`)). Large Sector 3 enemy turns still take 12+ seconds of waiting unless the player repeatedly presses Space/Enter to hurry, because `skip` resets to `false` at the end of every single enemy activation batch (`battle.gd:1370` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:1370`)).
  - Carrier squadrons fly and attack completely automatically in `swarmPhase` (`rules.gd:6764-6772` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:6764-6772`)), removing moment-to-moment agency from carrier fleets and adding extra passive watch time every round.

---

### 5. "24 Admirals, 6 Buttons" and thin tactical verb diversity across hulls
**Why it hurts:** The roster looks huge on paper (6 factions, 24 admirals, 51 hulls), but turn-to-turn verbs repeat heavily across admirals, hulls, and factions.

- **Source:** `ADMIRALS`, `CMD_POW`, `ABILITIES`, `ORDERS`, `HULLS`, `LEGACY` in `tables.json` (`godot/rules/data/tables.json`); `canOrder()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4570-4582`); `canAbility()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:6792-6811`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - All **24 admirals share only 6 Commands** (`barrage`, `hunt`, `scramble`, `iron`, `restore`, `surge`), differentiated at base level only by a small passive stat line (`+15% flank`, `+10% hull/shields`, `+8 evasion`).
  - All **51 hulls share only 13 abilities**, and `launch` is passive (`canAbility` returns `false` for players at `rules.gd:6796` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:6796`)). Two unlockable variants (`h_vanguard_g`, `c_hulk_g`) have `ab: null` (no active ability at all). Most hulls inside a faction copy the same button (`blink` on 4 Glasswright hulls, `phase` on 4 Eclipse hulls, `regrow` on 3 Chorus hulls), and most active abilities are pure self-stat buffs (`+30% dmg`, `+25 ev`, `restore 25% hull`) rather than spatial or combo tools.
  - Although `rules.gd:4570-4600` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4570-4600`) still has code for 4 orders (`brace`, `full`, `lock`, `helm`), only **1 order (`brace`)** is exposed in `ORDERS`, and Glasswrights cannot use even that (`FAC_GATES.ithar.noBrace`).
  - **Lopsided rosters:** Sunward Crusade has 6 base hull classes (Frigate to Dreadnought). Eclipse has only **3** playable base hulls (Frigate, Destroyer, Cruiser: no Carrier, no Battleship, no Dreadnought). Hullbreakers, Chorus, and Glasswrights have no Battleship or Dreadnought. Yet `LEGACY` sells `u_battleship` (60 renown, usable by only 2 of 6 factions) and `u_dread` (120 renown, Crusade only).

---

### 6. Boss fights are oversized skirmishes with no boss patterns or phases
**Why it hurts:** Sector bosses and the run finale are supposed to be the climax that tests your build and delivers adrenaline. Right now they are just a big HP-bar ship using normal AI.

- **Source:** `bossEncounter()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1050-1054`), `bossCmdTick()` & `bossCmdFire()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:5741-5763`), `checkEndRules()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4561-4567`), `BOSS_CMD` & `BOSS_ENC` in `tables.json` (`godot/rules/data/tables.json`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - `BOSS_ENC = ["rout", "rout", "ambush"]`: boss battles have no bespoke encounter mechanics; killing the boss hull immediately routes all escorts and ends the fight.
  - Every boss's sole special behavior is firing **one** of the exact same 5 player Commands (`barrage`, `surge`, `restore`, `iron`, `hunt`) **once per battle**, announced on round 2 (or below 60% HP) and firing the next round.
  - No multi-phase escalations, no telegraphed super-weapon lanes to dodge, no destructible sub-objectives or arena shifts, and no unique final-boss identity at the Hollow Sun.

---

### 7. Post-battle paperwork waterfall, unequipped loot chores, and a hidden salvage trap
**Why it hurts:** Winning a fight should feel fast and rewarding. Instead, victory launches a queue of modals, forces inventory housekeeping in another screen, uses the same word for two unrelated loot types, and secretly punishes factions for using their own weapons.

- **Source:** `rewardFlow()` through `promotionsStep()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3415-3742`), `salvageYield()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3472-3490`), `killCauseOf()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4163-4170`), `TERMS` (`godot/ui/campaign/campaign_ui.gd:39`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - **Modal queue:** One victory can chain up to **6 sequential modals**: Prize disposal -> Victory/Wreck salvage -> Protocol or Refit pick -> Relic pick (elite/boss) -> Captain promotions -> Story/Sector transition.
  - **Unequipped hold chore:** Refit modules stripped from wrecks (`campaign.gd:3582` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3582`)), picked as node rewards (`campaign.gd:3611` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3611`)), or bought at shipyards (`campaign.gd:2241` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:2241`)) drop into `RUN["inventory"]` unequipped, forcing a separate trip to the Fleet/Refits screen. Worse, if a ship dies in combat (`campaign.gd:3978-3985` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3978-3985`)), its fitted modules vanish forever instead of returning to salvage.
  - **Hidden faction anti-synergy trap:** `KILL_CAUSES` marks `big` (torpedoes, bombs, rams), `flay` (Eclipse null weapons), `melt` (Chorus bio-weapons), and `tidal` with `"scrap": 1`. In `salvageYield()` (`campaign.gd:3486-3490` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3486-3490`)), `"scrap": 1` sets `intact = false`, which **destroys the wreck's refit module (`m = null`) AND disables Hullbreaker towing (`tow = false`)**. Result: **Hullbreakers cannot tow or strip enemies they ram or torpedo** (their own core kit), and **Eclipse and Chorus almost never get intact modules from wrecks** because their entire faction arsenals trigger `flay`/`melt`. None of this is warned in battle.
  - **Term collision:** `TERMS` renames fleet-wide relics to **"salvage"**, while `REWARD_DEF` also calls post-battle wreck stripping **"salvage"**.

---

### 8. Upgrade bloat (stat soup over build pivots) and muted run tension
**Why it hurts:** Players juggle **11 separate in-run upgrade/economy tracks** (Credits/Biomass, CP, Ship Mk I-III, Class Tracks, Modules, Captain Perks, Wing Perks, Flagship Aspect, Protocols, Relics, Faction Verbs), yet most choices are small passive percentages (`+6%` to `+15%`), capped by 74 `FX_CAPS`, while the genuinely exciting combos are too rare to assemble in a short run.

- **Source:** `rollBoonOffer()` & `legendaryFor()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:724-770`), `genSector()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1071-1191`), `finishBattle()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3992-3995`), `checkEndRules()` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4528-4548`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - **Stat soup:** Ship Mk (`+20% hp/sh, +15% dmg`), Class Tracks (`+6% hp/dmg`), 13 of 14 Captain Perks (`+10 aim`, `+10% crit`, `+15% hp`), and 13 of 17 Modules are flat spreadsheet math with zero change to how you fly a turn.
  - **Synergy bottlenecks:** Only 62% of normal battles offer a Protocol (`campaign.gd:769` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:769`)), spread across 4 random cores. Legendaries (the actual build-defining capstones like chain explosions or shield-piercing lances) require `minR >= 1` (**elites and bosses only**), **2+ prior protocols from that specific core**, AND still lose a **45% coin flip** to a Duo (`campaign.gd:738,751-762` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:738`)). In a 3-sector run with only 4 branching columns per sector, you rarely get to enjoy a completed synergy engine for more than 2 or 3 fights.
  - **Softened stakes:** Every victory auto-heals **15% max HP** (`campaign.gd:3994` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3994`)) and every sector transition auto-heals **40%** (`campaign.gd:3765` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3765`)). Worse, **failing Hunt or Intercept still awards a `"win"`** (`B["over"] = "win"; B["partial"] = true`, `rules.gd:4531,4543` (`godot/rules/rules.gd:4531`)), keeping full salvage, protocols, XP, and map progress while only halving credit pay. Meanwhile, retreating costs only `10%` hull and drops you back on the previous node (`campaign.gd:3988,4042` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:3988`)). Attrition feels soft until a ship suddenly dies permanently and wipes its fitted gear.

---

### 9. Meta-progression fails both new and veteran players (bypassed by default, brutal grind when off, and 6 unobtainable unlocks)
**Why it hurts:** Good roguelike meta-progression feeds the "one more run" hook with exciting horizontal unlocks every 1 to 2 runs. Here it breaks in three opposite ways at once.

- **Source:** `campaign_ui.gd:112` (`godot/ui/campaign/campaign_ui.gd:112`), `title.gd:165-177` (`godot/main/title.gd:165-177`), `campaign.gd:49` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:49`), `campaign.gd:1204-1280` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1204-1280`), `campaign.gd:1748-1751` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1748-1751`), `campaign.gd:1856-1865` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1856-1865`), `campaign_ui.gd:908-944,1880` (`godot/ui/campaign/campaign_ui.gd:908-944`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - **Bypassed on launch:** `playtest_default = true` unlocks every admiral, carrier, battleship, hull variant, and all 8 lineage levels immediately on a fresh profile (and exposes a developer `"Test new battle maps..."` toggle in Run Options). A new player gets hit with maximum menu paralysis and zero unlock dopamine.
  - **Brutal grind when turned off:**
    - Full Renown unlock bill is **1,815 Renown** (`635` Legacy + `250` Variants + `930` for 18 Admirals), at `~101` Renown per full winning run and `~10-15` per Sector 1 loss.
    - **Respeccing an admiral's lineage tree between runs taxes permanent Renown** (`25 + 10 * respecs`, `campaign.gd:1273` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1273`)), directly punishing build experimentation.
    - **Per-admiral XP wall:** A full winning run pays `~41` XP (`campaign.gd:1857` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1857`)). First lineage pick = Level 5 (`75 XP`, ~2 wins). Capstone = Level 8 (`230 XP`, ~6 wins). Capstone Mastery III = **`600 XP` (~15 full wins with ONE admiral, across 24 admirals)**. The richest admiral identity mechanics are locked behind a massive grind wall.
  - **6 dead/unobtainable unlocks:** Progression tells players *"Finish the [Faction] story to unlock"* for 6 hull variants (`vs_penitent_l`, `h_interdictor_e`, `c_marauder_g`, `b_razor_e`, `i_carrier_a`, `d_jackal_h`), plus 6 flagship paints, medals, and Chronicle entries in `career.gd` (`godot/story/career.gd:69-91`). **But `arcs_on := false` (`campaign.gd:49` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:49`)) and `godot/story/data/arcs/` does not exist**, so those unlocks are unreachable without the playtest switch.
  - **Unrewarding difficulty ladder (`HEAT`):** UI text says *"Lose a run to unlock Threat"* (though `heatUnlocked()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:1332-1334`) unlocks on any win or loss), and Threat only adds passive enemy/price inflation for `+10%` extra Renown, with no new encounters, boss phases, or real endgame milestone.

---

### 10. Front-loaded onboarding walls and an under-realized Nemesis / narrative loop
**Why it hurts:** The first 5 minutes should drop a new player straight into a crisp, thrilling skirmish and teach through play. Instead, they wade through setup choices they lack context for, walls of tip text, and a Nemesis system that stops short of true rivalry.

- **Source:** `campaign_ui.gd:673-1025` (`godot/ui/campaign/campaign_ui.gd:673-1025`), `story.gd:121-126` (`godot/story/story.gd:121-126`), `campaign_tips.gd:6-12` (`godot/ui/campaign/campaign_tips.gd:6-12`), `battle.gd:78-88` (`godot/scenes/battle/battle.gd:78-88`), `campaign.gd:2688-2883` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:2688-2883`).
- **Exact logic:**
  - **Pre-battle gauntlet:** Title -> Command Desk (6 factions, 24 admirals, mastery bars, Lineage links, Run Options) -> Flagship Podium (forced to pick 1 of 3 permanent Flagship Refits before knowing what firing arcs, wings, or Command tiers even are) -> Sector Intro modal -> **"Name your flagship"** dialog -> 3D Map -> `c_map` tip card -> `c_clock` tip card -> Battle 1 -> up to 9 dense text teaching cards (`TIPS` in `battle.gd`).
  - **Nemesis stops short of personal drama:** Each sector forces exactly one meeting by Column 4 (`campaign.gd:2688-2695` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:2688-2695`)), and Sector 2/3 can swap to different rival factions (`nemAssign`). When he adapts at sector end (`nemAdapt()` (`godot/campaign/campaign.gd:2715-2735`)), the payoff is mostly a quiet passive stat boost (`+20% shields`, `+8 evasion`, `+10% armor`) rather than a visible tactical counter-fleet that forces a fresh plan.
  - **Career isolation:** `career.gd:3-4` (`godot/story/career.gd:3-4`) explicitly isolates medals, titles, and history from campaign/battle rules, and with `arcs_on := false`, the narrative layer feels disconnected from the core run loop.

---

## 3. Recommended Fix Priority (Highest Impact on Fun First)

| Priority | Change | Why It Moves the Needle Most |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Kill dynamic rubber-banding** | Remove `fleetPower()` budget scaling (`rules.gd:1639`) and `bossFit` boss HP shrinking (`rules.gd:1461`). Tune fixed, honest sector/node enemy budgets. | Immediately restores the entire roguelike power fantasy: upgrades, repairs, and combos finally feel worth earning. |
| **2. Fix battle feel & clarity** | Default `cine` cut-ins to **kills and boss Commands only** (never routine lances/torps). Keep `skip`/fast-pace sticky across a round. Add clear **next enemy activation + target intent** markers on the board. | Eliminates camera whiplash and waiting fatigue, and turns alternating activations into a sharp readable puzzle. |
| **3. Cut fake agency & bloat; deepen real choices** | Either wire real UI picking for `treeChoice` skills or rewrite them into honest active/positional mechanics. Collapse redundant passive stat tracks (Class Tracks + flat Mk bumps + tiny perk bumps) into fewer, punchier **build-pivoting** upgrades, and let Duos/Legendaries appear earlier in a run. | Replaces spreadsheet clutter and broken promises with genuine "oh awesome, look at this combo!" moments. |
| **4. Fix hidden loot traps & post-battle chore tax** | Remove `"scrap": 1` from faction weapons and Hullbreaker rams/torps (or reward *cleaner* kills with bonus credits instead of deleting modules/towing). Consolidate post-battle modals into one clean debrief/reward screen, let players fit won refits directly on the reward card, and give relics a distinct name from wreck salvage. | Removes unfair hidden penalties and cuts tedious between-battle clicking in half. |
| **5. Make bosses real bosses & overhaul meta cadence** | Give each sector boss 1 to 2 distinct mechanical patterns (telegraphed area hazards, phase shift at 50% HP, destructible hardpoints/summons). Turn off `playtestAll` for normal profiles, drop Lineage respec cost to 0, cut Admiral Lineage XP thresholds by ~3-4x (or unlock trees on Run 1-2), and ship/enable the 6 faction arcs so arc unlocks actually exist. | Gives every run an unforgettable climax and turns meta-progression into an addictive "one more run" loop instead of a grind wall. |

# Embers of the Hollow Sun: the rulebook

The index and shared rules for the whole project (issue 492, FINDINGS R190). Each rule says what to do, why (the problem
Ryan was reacting to, in his words where they exist), who set it and when, and its old ids. Rules of play and balance numbers
are not here (R190's scope): they live in the browser oracle, godot/rules and their FINDINGS rows (for example battles growing
over a run toward about 20 ships, a guide and not a cap, R1; capture as add, strip or ransom, R4).

Ryan, Nov 11 2026: "Those old hard coded rules with no context or detail artifically restricing us are exactly what I'm worried
about across the board" (R190), and at 20:05 CST: "Let's ensure we're documenting all these decisions and approaches. I don't
want this drift to keep happening or where we get confused on how we're doing things."

Set by: **Ryan** (his own call, his words exist), **Board** (a Claude Board thread wrote it), **agent** (Muse, Codex or a
worker). Ids are FINDINGS rows (R, D, F, G, X) or register ids from contrib/opus/reviews/rules_sweep/.

## 7. Movement

7.1 **Movement is never sudden, jerky or stop-start, and feels like space**: thrusters fire wherever a ship would need them
(braking, turning, stopping a turn, sliding). Why: "I don't want things to look jerky and the smooth call was because movement
was very stop/start and sudden. Thrusters should be involved when it makes sense on braking and turns." (R189). Set: Ryan,
Nov 11. Replaces the letter of R76 ("thruster puffs only on turns, no side-to-side shuffle"). Ids: R76a, R189a, movespec-01.

7.2 **The main engine does the travelling.** A one-hex sidestep or back-off may slide on thrusters; a longer run turns its nose
onto the course and burns the main engine; anything flown on thrusters alone is visibly slower and gentler. Why: "for one tile
over, it tracks but not when they're going like 3-10 tiles down just almost skating on thrusters" (R195). Set: Ryan, Nov 11.

7.3 **One ship moves at a time, at a weighty pace (about twice as slow as Nov 1); longer enemy turns are accepted; cinematic is
the default with a brisk option.** Why: "I don't want to sacrifice the feel of the game/space/the ships." (R50). Set: Ryan
(R50, R64); option Board (R50d). Ids: R50b, R50d, R64a, movespec-06.

7.4 **Movement playback never changes rules results.** A LOOK change keeps the route, end hex and facing; a RULE change (route
or facing) needs Ryan's own ruling and touches the Godot rules (R405). Why: R188's frame for the audit. Set: Board, Nov 11 (R188).

7.5 **No roll into turns.** Why: nothing in space leans a ship; the audit reversed the earlier bank (movement_audit_code.md).
Set: Board, Nov 11. Id: movespec-04 (the 4 degree bank, retired).

7.6 **Flip and burn stays off for now, to be looked at again now that braking jets are on screen.** Why: left alone on the
Board's advice (R193). Set: Ryan (R64, R193). Ids: R64c, feel-02.

7.7 **Every number in contrib/opus/briefs/movement_spec.md is a tuning value chosen by eye from motion strips.** Set: Board
(R189's rewrite). Ids: R131a, R131b, movespec-02, movespec-03, movespec-05, movespec-07.

7.8 **Strike craft move like small agile craft (quick turns, short burns), still never jerky.** Why: small craft should feel
quick, inside 7.1 (R189, R195). Set: Ryan (R55, R216).

7.9 **Firing ends a non-Glasswright ship's movement for that activation: no move, turn in place or ram after it fires.**
Glasswright ships keep their post-fire move budget, and a turn after firing spends it. Admiral tree skills that hand out
movement after firing (Fleet Elsewhere, The Wall Moves) add to that same budget. A free turn granted by an admiral tree skill
(Cut and Turn, Fleet Elsewhere, Trophy Standard) still turns a ship after firing; that skill is the exception it grants (Set:
Ryan, Nov 22, R397). Why:
Ryan, "Agree no" (issue 1560 item 14) and "Yes agree on skills". Set: Ryan, Nov 22 (R396, R397). Code: canRotate and ramInfo in both rules twins.

rising whooshes or stock explosions; weight in the low and low-mid with a soft top. Why: "The sounds that I've heard from the
game so far are bad" (R163). Set: Ryan (R163, R171). Ids: R171b, program-13, sound-01, sound-03.

8.2 **Weapons stay dry; big moments get weight**: deaths, capital hits and shield breaks get tails, sub-bass, a bed for the

Board's reword, Ryan's go (R187, R193). Id: sound-02.

8.3 **The gun chooses the sound of its hit**, by weapon and by what it struck. Why: one family of hit clips played whatever
fired (audit item 8). Set: Ryan's go (R193); built in issue 506.

(reworded from "at least four"). Id: sound-04.

## 4. Ships and concepts

4.1 **Space ships, never sea ships, in the whole shape.** No boat profile, keel, raked prow, deck house, mast, funnel, crane,
railings, porthole rows or anything hanging off; a worked belly. Why: Ryan, Oct 22: "careful that these don't stretch into
obvious naval-looking ships. again, these are SPACE ships"; Nov 11: "I don't understand the random things hanging off, it reads
as naval. We need to do a full pass across all ships and factions so not naval" (R185). Set: Ryan (Oct 22, Oct 24, R185). Ids:
agents-19, agents-25, R8b, R185a, concepts-16. Detail: docs/playbooks/concepts_round2.md gate line 11.

4.2 **No gun faces backward or into the ship at rest; a turret may turn aft only to follow a target its rules arc lets it hit
(6.16, R222).** Why: "no ship in the game fires backward" (Oct 22). Set: Ryan (Oct 22; the turret line Nov 12, R222).
Ids: agents-17, blob-03, R222.

4.3 **Parts look like they belong: snapped to the real hull on a visible mount, in matched pairs at sensible hard points; the
Hullbreakers may be junky.** Why: bolt-ons on the AI hulls floated, sank or sat anywhere (Oct 21). Set: Ryan, Oct 21. Ids:
agents-18, agents-24, factions-02.

4.4 **A ship reads as armed from above at thumbnail size; each faction mounts its forward weapon its own way, never a long
barrel on the nose tip; no two factions share an outline from above; identity shows under the battle camera.** Why: "It's
really hard to tell if there's any guns right now so it barely looks like a warship" (R176); "same giant gun directly on nose.
It's good to have forward facing but it always looks the same across factions" (R183). Set: Ryan's complaints; wording Board
(R176, R183). Ids: R176b, R183a, R183b, concepts-04, concepts-05.

4.5 **Every faction is its own: its own parts kit and shape language; only invisible plumbing is shared.** Why: "all the
factions are supposed to be unique and different. Having the same parts everywhere is against that" (R151). Set: Ryan. Ids:
R151b. The faction sheets (shape, colour, where guns sit, how it breaks, its Never list) are docs/playbooks/factions.md.

4.6 **One concept style for every faction: realistic and detailed, like a photograph of a real built object**
(contrib/muse/design/concept_directions_2026_11/corsair_A.jpg); a picture that reads as an illustration, a toy or a cartoon
fails. Ryan judges the style, side by side; the Board never declares it. Why: "Pretty realistic and detailed to help with the
builds... this style is how it should look in game" (R197); "It's semi realistic but not quite" (R198). Set: Ryan, Nov 11.

4.7 **When Ryan likes a picture, the next image job edits that picture**; colour alone never sends a picture back; when image
rounds cannot reach the style without breaking the shape, stop and use the Opus build-sheet route. Why: six Hullbreaker rounds
were lost redescribing a liked picture in words (R192); "we can fix color ourselves rather than get stuck in a loop with color
fixes with image generation" (R204). Set: Ryan and Board, Nov 11 (R192, R204, R206).

4.8 **No generated concept reaches a build, or Ryan, without the Board's review against the written gate**
(docs/playbooks/concepts_round2.md). The gate's ratios and fractions (proportions per class, the stern fraction) are starting
points for a drawing, not identity. Why: "I need you to do a much more in depth review and refinement before these ever go to
actual builds" (R172); Hegemony's 4.5 : 1 was overruled by R183's 3 : 1. Set: Ryan (R172); the ratio note Board. Ids: R172a,
R172b, concepts-08, concepts-14.

4.9 **Start from what was already liked.** Why: two rounds were lost designing the Glasswrights and Hullbreakers afresh and
sanding off what made them theirs (R180). Set: Board lesson after Ryan's review (R180). Ids: R180c, factions-17.

4.10 **The finished battle is Sunward Crusade against Eclipse, on the dead-star board.** Why: one finished fight proves every
recipe and is the reference for later jobs (R167: "I want this to end with something that opus or other models can run
from"). Set: Ryan (R167, R180). Ids: R167b, R180d, handoff-01.

4.11 **Every part has a job and every weapon is its faction's own.** A part with no purpose is cut; weapons, turrets and
launchers are designed per faction from the lore bible and the faction sheet (how the weapon works shows in its mount,
housing, barrel and muzzle), never a shared silhouette; a gun in another weapon's firing lane or backblast is a clash. Why:
Ryan on the Hullbreakers: "let's get rid of the chains randomly around the ship. There's no purpose" and "a gun directly
behind the rocket pods on a16 ... seems like it conflicts"; on Eclipse: "their turrets look the same as hullbreakers" (R221).
Set: Ryan, Nov 12 (R221). Parts carry the hull's detail density: triangles and edge features per square unit, per part
type, within 25 percent of the hull's, reported on every sheet (R224: "They also just look smoother and less detailed, maybe
slightly less poly than the rest of the ship").

## 5. Ship build pipeline

5.1 **No ship is built until its build sheet passes the concept standard** (contrib/muse/design/concept_standard_2026_11/standard.md:
true side and top at one scale, underside, bow-on, length from game data, scale bar, a feature table that outranks the
pictures). Why: "I want to make sure that they are good enough to actually hand build from in blender" (R203). Set: Ryan,
Nov 11.

5.2 **The concept guides the build; it is not traced.** The Opus builder is the designer of record: it keeps the picture's
identity (mass, outline from above, character, palette, where the big features sit), fixes what would not work as a built
object, takes guns from the hull's data.js slots as batteries that make sense, carries every tier and change of height the
picture shows, and lists every change on the sheet. Why: "Use it to guide, not the very final exact design" (R207); "The guns
look randomly placed and don't make sense... the builds look like square blocks basically" and "The concept should inform and
guide but it's not a final play by play guide" (R213). Set: Ryan, Nov 11. Ids: R25 (concepts are inspiration), R207, R213.
The Board (Opus) is the final designer and director; Muse concepts. Between an accepted concept and the build the Board makes
the design calls, family distinctness included (a class that reads as a small copy of another class from above is changed in
the build), lists them on the sheet and shows Ryan the result instead of asking first. Ryan's picks of concepts and his
verdicts on pictures stand. Why: "You're the final designer and director. Muse is just concepting" (R233). Set: Ryan, Nov 12.

5.3 **The settled build method is binding** (docs/playbooks/ships.md section 0; docs/ship_pipeline/RECIPE.md): the hull designed
on the approved build sheet (5.1, 5.2), which the recipe builds as it is and never traces again (issue 592), with the stage 2
AI shape reference made from the accepted concept as an outline and grime reference only, never shipped; hand-built parts, AI parts only through a reviewed faction
library; paint from geometry masks, trim sheets and decals, never projected concept art; the seven stages. Why: projected
concept paint was dropped on all 36 hulls (R82); Ryan adopted the research route (R96); the method kept drifting between
documents (R214). Set: Ryan (R82, R96, R214, R215). Ids: R82d, R96a, R96c, R150a.

5.4 **Breakable by design, with comprehensive, detailed insides.** Every hull has real thickness and insides through the whole hull
(decks, frames, spaces, machinery; Chorus flesh and bone; Glasswright layered glass), rim bands and a dark liner where the
intact ship shows; the build check fails a hull whose broken pieces show a hollow or flat inside. Starting with the Blender
Interior Kit V2 (issue 1743, R416 Layer 3), new ship builds and rebakes replace plain untextured chamfered boxes and flat slabs
with modeled interior modules (ribbed decks, framed arch bulkheads, cylindrical reactors/turbines/racks, sculpted organic sacs
and bone struts, collared crystal waveguides), UV-mapped to a shared per-faction interior trim atlas (`albedo`, `normal`, `orm`,
optional `emission`, supported by `tools/recipe/export7.py`) and verified by a build-sheet cutaway render while staying 0 px
clean on `surface_check.py`. Hulls built before this rule rely on the runtime Wounds V2 triplanar interior shader and breach-mouth
3D dressing (issue 1741) or, for legacy hollow hulls, the game-side interior fallback (issue 167). Why: "the broken open pieces
are visibly empty" (R98); "so we don't run into the issues of before with just empty looking husks" (R209); "I think it's
better to be comprehensive with internal if we can without performance issues" (R215); auditing all 45 ships under R416 showed
plain untextured boxes and flat slabs behind the hull skin (Ryan, Nov 22). Set: Ryan, Nov 4, 11 and 22. Ids: R70, R98a, R98b,
R99a, R209, R215, R416.

5.5 **Breaks follow the faction's rule and the class, never a fixed count or a straight cut**; hard points and breach anchors
scale with class and faction, read from one table (factions.md; the check reads it, issue 363). Why: "is 28 hard points for
every ship? It should vary by size of ship, faction, etc. We want things to be on theme." (R164); wrecks must look blown
apart (R186). Set: Ryan (R164, R186, R215). R99 Q2 (two transverse lines plus one longitudinal) and AGENTS.md's "two or three
break lines" are retired. Ids: R164d, R99b, R98b, ships-07, factions-04.

5.6 **Hand-built parts carry the hull's level of surface detail.** Why: "the level of texture and details seem to vary wildly"
(Oct 21). Set: Ryan. Id: agents-28.

5.7 **Structure first: the massing carries the concept's variety of shape before any detail.** Why: "There's so much less
variety in the shape and structure of it, so it's not just adding but almost removal." (R140). Set: Ryan, Nov 9. Ids: R140,
R213.

5.8 **The outline overlap against the concept is reported, not a pass bar** (was 90 percent, R147). Why: the builder is told
to depart from the picture where it does not work (R207), and a 90 percent pass let a wrong bow through (R157). Set: Board,
Nov 11 (reworded). Ids: R147, ships-05, recipe-03.

5.9 **The blob sweep (nine cells: bow, midship, stern from top, side and below) is a viewing instrument for Ryan's eye, not a
pass bar.** Why: assumed gates stop binding until measured (R121). Set: Ryan (R121d). Ids: agents-27, ships-08, blob-01.

5.10 **The guns are never bent to fit a score.** Why: casemate barrels had been bent to raise the outline match (R156). Set:
Ryan ("I agree with all of your takes", R156). Id: R156a.

5.11 **Every recipe stage is one double-click, stops on its own failure with a non-zero exit, deletes nothing, and stage 7
copies aside what it replaces before copying into the game.** Why: Ryan is not a coder; missing things fail loudly (R158).
Set: Board and Muse's conditions (R158). Ids: recipe-01, recipe-02, recipe-08.

5.12 **Ship assets ship as glb copied into the PC build; .vsm belongs to the frozen browser game.** Why: Godot cannot load
.vsm. Set: Board (G-9, G-11).

5.13 **Assets only under CC0 (Kenney, KayKit, Poly Haven, ambientCG); Quaternius is out.** Why: its licence is not CC0 (D11).
Set: Board. Ids: D11, X14.

5.14 **A build pull request carries its done-when evidence and a method line** (build sheet link, manifest, budget numbers,
changes made to the sheet); the outside check returns one without them as blocking. Why: R214. Set: Ryan, Nov 11.

5.15 **Parts read as what they are and fit together: the fit check.** Engines are bells with throats and rings, guns have a base,
mantlet, breech and muzzle, launch tubes have depth; the bow and big masses carry the concept's shaping. No part inside
another, in another gun's arc, in an exhaust cone or blocking a launcher; a fit view and fit report on every sheet and build.
Why: round 2 sheets had guns blocking rockets and in front of an engine, tubes as flat circles, engines and guns as plain
tubes, and a flat-block bow (Ryan, Nov 11, R217). Set: Ryan, Nov 11 (R217). Ids: ships-2c.

5.16 **Fidelity is whole-ship: a parts inventory, one detail level, kit first, region by region.** Every feature the concept
shows is listed with its sub-parts and modelled; every part sits at the same detail level as its neighbours; each faction's
kit holds every part type at that level; the fit check covers every part; the sheet ticks the inventory per blob-sweep cell
beside the concept. Feedback on one part becomes a rule for all parts. Why: "Engines and guns are the reference but we want
to carry that through to the whole model. Don't just patch singular behavior or examples, use it for global learning and
shaping the approach" (Ryan, Nov 11, R218). Set: Ryan, Nov 11 (R218). Ids: ships-2c.

5.17 **A machine never crosses a seam; structure that crosses a seam is torn at it, insides included.** Guns, turrets,
casemates, launchers, engines, thrusters, claws and sensor masts ride whole with one piece: the seam moves, or kinks round
them in plan. Hull plating, frames, ribs, rails, openings such as a launch bay, and every inside (decks, bulkheads, rooms,
the liner) tear across a seam, along the same ragged line as the plating over them: no inside panel stays whole across a
break or sticks out past its piece's broken hull. The stage 4 audit reads each part's kind from the build (the faction kit's
MACHINES) and fails only a machine across a seam; the export carries each seam's path and each machine's box, and the game's
death cut reads them there (fx/test/death_seam_check.gd: zero machines split, zero insides outside their piece). Why: a cut
gun reads as sliced, a torn plate as blown apart (R186, "blown apart, never sliced"); whole deck and bulkhead slabs stuck out
of the broken A16 as big flat squares (Ryan, Nov 12, issue 600). Set: Board, Nov 12 (R226; insides added from Ryan's eye,
issue 600). Ids: ships-2c.

5.18 **The ship detail standard: textures by size, AO and LODs on import, one authored look, full hard points.** For every
ship from now on: (1) stage 7 exports maps by the ship's length band, flagships and battleships (length 21 and up) at 4096
(stage 5 already bakes 4096), cruisers, carriers, destroyers and frigates (6.5 to 16.5) at 2048, strike craft (1.6) at 1024
(issue 1680); (2) every hull gets a calibrated `ao_light_affect` (never Godot's default 0.0; per faction in look.gd READ, 0.35
to 0.55, Glasswrights 0.2) and automatic Godot mesh LODs on import (issues 1678, 1679); (3) each faction's paint stack moves
to `authored_look = 1`, calibrated to the one battle light rig, the next time that faction is baked or repainted, and its
look.gd READ albedo lift (Navy 0.4x, Eclipse 2.2x and the rest) retires with it; (4) every new destroyer and larger carries
`hp_rcs` and `hp_board` hard points, plus articulated turrets where the faction uses them. Comparison sheets go on Ryan's Pick
Sheet; GPU captures only after green checks and Artoo (3.12). Why: hero hulls were downsampled to 2048 while fighters carried
39 MB of maps, baked seam AO vanished under the key light, and each faction leaned on a different after-the-fact lift
(Ryan's Ship Graphical Detail and Consistency Upgrade Plan). Set: Ryan, Nov 22 2026 (R411). Replaces the Nov 19 park of
far-away LODs until a speed check (R328 notes, issue 1152) and, for the game, issue 592's "the game loads no LOD chain":
stage 6's hand chain stays an analysis product, the game makes its own LODs at import.

</file>

Read the [PC playbook](../../docs/playbooks/pc.md) before changing or running the queue, watchdog, or job wrappers. RULEBOOK sections 3.2 to 3.4 and 3.12 cover shared PC and GPU limits.

## 3.5 to 3.7. PC harness

3.5 **Every PC queue job is wrapped in the tmo.bat watchdog, ends with exit /b, and carries no |, &, < or > in its
arguments.** Agent runs stop after STALL_MIN minutes without progress (default 30), or at a hard ceiling (default six
hours; CODEX_CAP and WORK_CAP override the ceiling in seconds). Progress is a changed file write time in the run repo,
a new commit, or new bytes in log.txt (also stderr for workhorse runs). Git housekeeping does not count. A stall or ceiling
stop writes its reason, changed files and last log lines to the out folder's resume.txt and the -partial commit message;
the next run reads that note. timeouts.log records STALLED after N min or CEILING. Short queue commands and runner checks
keep their explicit time limits. Why: hung Godot windows blocked the queue for about three hours (G-3), but the old two-hour
agent cap killed jobs that were still working (367 and 371). Ryan, Nov 15: "do we need to get rid of that random 2 hour rule
if it's timing out actual work?" He took up a stall check, a high backstop and a saved resume note (issue 818). Set: Board
(G-3), Ryan (issue 818). Ids: G-3, feel-06, skill-pb-05.

PC jobs never use Ryan's real game profile. The watchdog gives each Godot start a fresh profile so captures cannot overwrite his settings (issue 1228, Nov 19).

PC jobs run one tools copy and report honestly (issue 1194, Board, Nov 20). `lane_tools_refresh.ps1 -Build tools_live`
installs main's tools as a verified, never-edited version under `Downloads\voidsworn_test\tools_live\` with its own
hashes, named by `tools_live\current.txt`; every `tmo.bat` outside it hands its step to that copy, so an old `build\tools`
or branch checkout never runs its own watchdog or slot reader (self-tests set `TMO_OWN_COPY=1`). The main watcher refreshes
tools_live and `build\tools` between jobs. Old lane backups and old tools_live versions rotate instead of stopping the
refresh: a backup goes only when every file in it is kept in a newer copy or a saved main snapshot, a version only when it
was replaced over a day ago and no running process names it (the refresh's own rebuildable copies, 3.3). Job bats run
their steps through `tools/pc/job_wrap.bat`: a GPU label on every claim, the tool preflight before any clone or GPU claim
(exit 2 on a missing tool), the strict watchdog hash check, a stop on a failed step unless it is marked optional, non-empty
declared outputs, and `done PASS` or `done FAILED: <steps>` then `all done`, with a non-zero exit after any failure. Helper
(Opus) proof bats start from `tools/pc/jobs/opus_job_template.bat` and call `opus_job_head.bat` from tools_live: exact
commit pins in a fresh checkout per attempt, the safe ships copy with a tracked-file check, the throwaway profile and
Ryan's options hashed before and after; the Board checks only that a bat calls the head (docs/playbooks/pc.md, issue
1303, Board Nov 20: seven bats sent back on Nov 19 and 20 for the same four mistakes). The
